title: Israel's Election Hands No One a Mandate as Washington Readies a Post-Midterm Strike Package on Iran
subhead: With 85 percent of Israeli ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc holds 53 seats and the opposition 48 — no majority for either — while the White House has told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the November 3 midterms, and Brent settles above $115 after a Houthi missile claim against Saudi Arabia's largest refinery.

sections.heading: Israel Votes: A Fragmented Result and a Military That Refuses to Be Drawn In
sections.body:
Partial official results with 85.6 percent of votes counted put Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot at 48, according to the Central Elections Committee figures carried by Xinhua and The Times of Israel. Arab-led parties hold a projected 19 seats. About half a million double-envelope ballots from military bases, hospitals and other institutions remain uncounted, with the count due to finish by Friday.

Likud declared the election 'stolen by Arab parties who support terrorism', alleging corruption, threats and the use of prohibited software — an allegation the Joint List's Ahmad Tibi dismissed to Al Jazeera as 'the rhetoric of the defeated'. Defence Minister Israel Katz attacked Eisenkot for telling the military not to obey political direction from Netanyahu, calling it anti-democratic. Eisenkot, for his part, said Netanyahu is a caretaker premier without a mandate and told him not to use Israel's security for political needs.

The coalition arithmetic is unusually open. Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen told Reuters his party would use its projected 12 seats to help remove Netanyahu but would not join an Eisenkot-led government over its support for the Gaza campaign and the occupation of southern Lebanon; he left open backing such a government from outside. Ra'am's Mansour Abbas has said he would join an Eisenkot-led government.
sections.whyItMatters: A caretaker government with no majority is the weakest possible position from which to launch or sustain a new war with Iran. The open dispute between the defence minister and the opposition candidate over whether the military answers to the prime minister is not routine election noise — it is a signal that the command chain is being politicised at the exact moment strike decisions are pending.

sections.heading: Washington Signals a Post-Midterm Offensive; Tehran Says the Mediation Is Not an Offer
sections.body:
The Wall Street Journal reported that the US has warned several Gulf Arab states to prepare for a short, intense military offensive against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, though people briefed on the conversations said Trump has not made a final decision. Separately, the Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance — acting on Trump's direction, per one source — sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, focused on a framework for talks rather than the substance of a deal. CNBC and Reuters both linked the oil move to the same report.

On the mediation track, Reuters reported that Qatari mediators presented Tehran with a new draft on Sunday, a seven-day sequenced plan with daily confidence-building steps and multiple guarantors, with a response expected by the end of the week. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Doha had put forward 'unacceptable ideas and not an offer', and that Tehran's refusal to show flexibility on the nuclear file was unchanged. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran remained in close contact with intermediaries and that its own seven-day plan could be implemented in less than a week.

The gap is structural and clearly stated: Washington wants the nuclear programme inside the talks from the outset; Tehran wants the US naval blockade of Iranian ports lifted and sanctions on oil exports removed first.
sections.whyItMatters: Both tracks are running at once — a letter aimed at reviving talks and a warning to Gulf hosts to prepare for war — and neither is close to closing. The sequencing dispute (nuclear first versus sanctions relief first) is the actual deadlock, and the midterms are now the operative deadline for whichever way Washington goes.

sections.heading: Yemen: Aden Airport Hit Twice, a Saudi Refinery Claimed, Brent Settles at $115
sections.body:
Two ballistic missiles struck the perimeter of Aden airport on Wednesday, wounding civilians and causing damage, according to government forces spokesman Majed Abdullah Al-Nazili, who described it as the sixth such attack on the facility. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree had called on people at the airport to evacuate, saying a Saudi military cargo plane was present. Earlier, Houthi broadcaster Almasirah reported 14 dead and 15 wounded in strikes it attributed to Saudi Arabia on a market and a petrol station in Jawf province. AP reported the same toll from Houthi sources.

On Tuesday the Houthis said they had hit Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, Ras Tanura — a 550,000-barrel-per-day facility. Saudi authorities had not confirmed the strike at the time of reporting, per Reuters. Brent settled up $1.44, or 1 percent, at $115.32 a barrel, with WTI up 3 percent at $102.78. Reuters noted the Brent gain pushed the contract into overbought territory for the fourth time in five days. Gulf equities ended mixed on the Ras Tanura claim.

Yemeni government forces said they carried out 749 attacks on Houthi positions across multiple fronts in 24 hours, per a statement cited by Xinhua — a scale of claimed activity that signals the Yemeni civil war has fully re-fused with the wider regional conflict.
sections.whyItMatters: The Houthis have moved from disrupting Red Sea shipping to striking the world's largest crude exporter's most important refinery and the seat of Yemen's recognised government. That is a different war from the one that began in February, and the market is pricing it as such. If Ras Tanura damage is confirmed, the supply-side story stops being about a closed strait and becomes about physical damage to Saudi export capacity.

sections.heading: Ukraine: A Local Ceasefire Holds While Russia Hits Bridges and Romania Confronts a Sabotage Network
sections.body:
The US-brokered ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, in Kherson Oblast, has held into its second day. Marc Beckman, senior adviser to First Lady Melania Trump, told the Kyiv Independent that Putin 'wanted very much' for her to mediate and wrote a formal letter naming her as Russia's exclusive intermediary, and that the Russian military proposed moving the truce forward two days and extending its geographic scope within Kherson Oblast for aid deliveries and evacuations — a proposal Ukraine accepted.

Elsewhere, the picture is escalation rather than de-escalation. Russian strikes damaged a university campus and Kyiv's Southern Bridge; a Ukrainian military source told Reuters the bridge was hit by four Iskander ballistic missiles. Zelensky called it 'a serious escalation' against Ukrainian logistics, and Kyiv's mayor said the city will allocate 1 billion hryvnias ($22m) to build water crossings over the Dnipro. Russian strikes also killed 2 and injured 17 in other regions over the past day, per the Kyiv Independent.

On the European flank, Romanian President Nicusor Dan called an alleged Russian sabotage plot a 'grave violation' of a NATO member's sovereignty, after Romanian intelligence identified a Russia-coordinated sabotage network tied to a fire in Brasov County; three foreign nationals are under investigation and Bucharest summoned Russia's ambassador. France has relocated a maritime patrol aircraft to Romania, where at least eight cargo ships have been hit near Romanian and Bulgarian coasts in three weeks, with about 34 sailors dead or missing. Poland will host the only Patriot maintenance centre outside the US, per its deputy defence minister.

Diplomatically, Zelensky said he expects trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi by November 10, without a firm date, as the Netherlands announced a 500 million euro package and the UK announced a $13 billion 2027 support package.
sections.whyItMatters: The Oleshky truce is a genuine and unusual development — a Russian-requested, First Lady-brokered local ceasefire that expanded in scope — but it is running in parallel with an intensifying campaign against Ukrainian bridges and logistics. The Romanian sabotage case is the more consequential item for Europe: it turns Russian hybrid activity from an abstract warning into a named intelligence finding on NATO territory.

sections.heading: The First Island Chain Gets a Name and a Doctrine
sections.body:
Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met in Cebu on the sidelines of the ASEAN defence meetings and agreed on efforts to 'implement an effective denial defence in the First Island Chain' — the arc running from Japan through Taiwan to the Philippines — according to the US Defence Department, as reported by The Straits Times. Koizumi briefed Hegseth on Japan's work to update its national security strategy and related documents by the end of 2026.

The day before, Japan's Defence Ministry announced that a China Coast Guard vessel had accompanied three Chinese naval ships — including two guided-missile destroyers — through the Osumi Strait off Kagoshima into the Pacific. Kyodo and the ministry noted it was the first time Japan had publicly disclosed a Coast Guard ship escorting navy vessels through a strait near Japan. Japan's Maritime Self-Defense Force monitored the transit.

Taiwan's defence minister separately accused Beijing of weaponising the anniversary of the island's 1945 handover, citing satellite imagery of Taipei and fighter jet footage released as 'cognitive warfare', per the Taipei Times. The US House version of the Taiwan Security Initiative would provide $1 billion, while the Senate version authorises the Pentagon to build a war-reserve plan for Taiwan, per China Times.
sections.whyItMatters: 'Effective denial defence in the First Island Chain' is a doctrinal commitment to hold the line at the maritime geography rather than defend from behind it, and it now has both governments' names on it. The Chinese Coast Guard escorting navy destroyers through a Japanese strait is the matching signal from the other side: Japan's outermost maritime boundary is being normalised as transit space.

sections.heading: Spain: A Rail Disaster and a Political Reckoning
sections.body:
Two high-speed trains collided in Toledo province in central Spain, killing at least 68 people and injuring more than 100, according to Euronews and Xinhua. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez declared three days of national mourning from the emergency command post near the site and pledged a thorough investigation, saying the government would act firmly if negligence or failures in railway safety systems were found. Euronews reported grief, protests and calls for resignations in the aftermath.

In Brazil, Flávio Bolsonaro — defeated by Lula in Sunday's runoff, which AP reported with 100 percent of votes counted — arrived in Miami via Argentina and Ecuador, AFP reported. Bolsonaro had rejected the result.
sections.whyItMatters: Europe's deadliest rail accident in years lands on a Spanish government already under pressure, and the protest demand for resignations converts a safety failure into a governing crisis. The Bolsonaro departure to Florida adds a second contested-election exit to the hemisphere's politics, echoing the pattern of incumbents leaving under protest rather than conceding.

bottomLine: Today's central fact is that nobody can decide anything: Israel has voted no majority to either bloc, Iran has called the Qatari draft not an offer, and Washington has warned Gulf states to prepare for strikes it says it has not yet ordered. The Oleshky truce is real and held through a second day, but it is a local humanitarian arrangement, not a peace process, and Russia spent the same period putting four Iskander missiles into a Kyiv bridge. Watch three dates: Friday's completion of Israel's count, the November 3 US midterms, and Tehran's promised response to Qatar by week's end. If the Israeli count produces a caretaker government and the Iranian answer is another rejection, the post-midterm strike option becomes the path of least resistance rather than a threat.
